title: The influence of different radiation techniques on the quality of life and the functional and psychosocial rehabilitation of patients with carcinoma of the oropharynx
summary: The aim of the planned study is to investigate the influence of modern radiotherapy techniques on the quality of life and the functional and psychosocial rehabilitation of patients with oral and pharyngeal carcinoma. New radiation techniques (Intensity Modulation Radiation Therapy (IMRT)) allow a more focused alignment of the radiation field to the target region. Compared to older methods (conventional irradiation), healthy tissue can be spared. It is planned to compare the data sets of a multicentre, retrospective study (DÖSAK study on the rehabilitation of patients with oral cancer, conformational irradiation), which were collected before the year 2000, with current data (IMRT).
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx

interventions.name:
Data from Patients with IMRT 
questionnaires concerning functional and psychosocial outcomes and quality of life following IMRT (Bochum Questionnaire on Rehabilitation), EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-H&N35 and OHIP-G

Data from patients with conventional irradiation 
questionnaires concerning functional and psychosocial outcomes and quality of life following conventional irradiation  (Bochum Questionnaire on Rehabilitation)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
radio-oncological therapy of carcinoma of the oropharynx in the last 6 months to 5 years,
Age of patients ≥18 years,
the ability to complete German-language questionnaires
verbal and written consent
Exclusion criteria:
lack of agreement of the patient,
missing dental findings pre-RTX,
Age of patients <18 years,
lack of knowledge of German to complete the questionnaires
